# Smart home - statistics & facts

Smart homes use connected appliances, sensors, and control hubs to automate daily routines, enhance residential security, and optimize household energy consumption. By integrating Internet of Things (IoT) hardware, generative AI voice assistants, and standardized cross-platform protocols such as Matter and Thread, connected living has moved from early-adopter gadgets into mainstream residential infrastructure. Counting households equipped with at least one connected device or smart TV, the global number of smart homes surpassed 1.58 billion in 2025 and is forecast to reach 1.68 billion in 2026 before climbing to 1.94 billion by 2029. Household adoption is highest in mature digital economies, with the U.S. smart home penetration rate reaching nearly 90 percent, ahead of the United Kingdom at 87.8 percent and Germany at 81.4 percent. 

## Tech ecosystems and appliance manufacturers converge

Platform ecosystems from Amazon, Google, and Apple have driven consumer adoption mainly through voice-enabled smart speakers and displays, which serve as the central command hub for connected residences. This hardware foundation supports a global smart speaker market projected to grow from 22.1 billion U.S. dollars in 2025 to 24 billion in 2026 and 31.5 billion by 2030, as annual smart speaker sales expand from 254.4 million units in 2025 to 281.3 million in 2026. On the white-goods and robotics side, Chinese manufacturers play a dominant manufacturing role: Haier Smart Home solidified its position among the world's largest appliance makers with annual revenues of 302.4 billion yuan in 2025, while specialized domestic brands such as Roborock, Ecovacs, and Dreame lead the global robotic cleaning market.

## Entertainment, appliances, and residential security lead spending

Consumer adoption varies noticeably across device categories and regions. In China, a 2026 consumer survey shows that 63 percent of respondents already use smart appliances such as robot vacuums and connected kitchen devices, followed by 54 percent using smart lighting and power controls and 47 percent owning smart speakers. Globally, connected home entertainment and major appliances generate the highest commercial value, with the worldwide smart appliances segment generating over 50.2 billion U.S. dollars in annual revenue and projected to add nearly 16 billion U.S. dollars through 2031. Residential safety represents another mass-market pillar, with smart home security systems such as connected cameras and smart locks active in 953.1 million households worldwide in 2026 and heading past 1.07 billion by 2029.

## Smart energy management and grid electrification

Beyond convenience and security, volatile electricity prices, residential heat pumps, and rooftop solar integration are turning connected thermostats and smart meters into essential household infrastructure. As connected energy management systems expand to 561.8 million households worldwide in 2026 and 635.2 million by 2029, automated load shifting is becoming a core building block of residential decarbonization.
